The Sages taught It once happened that Rabbi Akiva was incarcerated in a prison, and Rabbi Yehoshua HaGarsi would attend to his Every day would bring him water in a measured One day the prison guard met said to him: your water today is more perhaps you need in order to undermine the prison. He said to him: What can I do; for one is liable to death better that I should die my own death rather than transgress the opinion of my colleagues They said he would not taste anything until brought him water and he washed his hands. When the Sages heard about this, they said: If in his old age so how much more so in his youth. if in prison so how much more so when not in prison. When he was crossing a river a ferry, the wind blew and cast it into the water, a fish swallowed it. was removed it was brought nightfall on Shabbat eve. said: Who buys like this? said to Go bring it to Yosef who cherishes Shabbat, as he regularly purchases They brought it to him he purchased it. He ripped found a pearl inside it. He sold it for thirteen vessels filled with golden dinars This elderly man encountered him and said: One who lends Shabbat, Shabbat repays him. The Sages taught: Once all the Jewish people ascended for pilgrimage Festival to Jerusalem and there was not water for them to drink. Nakdimon ben Guryon, a certain officer [<i>hegemon</i>] said to him: Lend me twelve wells of water for the pilgrims, and I will give back to you twelve wells of water. At noontime sent to him: Send me either water or coins that you owe me. sent to him: I still have left in the day. sent to him: Send me either water or coins that you owe me. sent to him: I still have left in the day. That officer ridiculed him, saying: the entire year rain has not fallen, and now it will rain? He entered the bathhouse in joy, As the master entered the bathhouse in his joy, Nakdimon entered the Temple in sadness. He wrapped himself and stood in prayer. He said before Master of the Universe, it is revealed and known before You that I did not act for my own honor, nor did I act for the honor of my father’s house. Rather, I acted for Your honor, so that there should be water for the Festival pilgrims. Immediately the sky became overcast and rain fell until the twelve cisterns were filled with water, and they overflowed. As the master left the bathhouse, Nakdimon ben Guryon left the Temple. An incident which Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, came from Migdal Gedor, from his rabbi’s house, and he was riding on a donkey and strolling on the bank of the river. What is pestilence? a city that sends out five hundred infantrymen, The Sages taught: a city that sends out fifteen hundred infantrymen, the village of Akko, and nine dead are removed from it on three consecutive days, this is pestilence. on a single day, or over four days, this is not pestilence. And a city that sends out five hundred infantrymen, for example, the village of Amiko, and three dead are removed from it on three consecutive days, this is pestilence. on one day or over four days, pestilence. Drokart sent out five hundred infantrymen, and three dead were removed from it on one day. What between a priest and the daughter of a priest? The meal-offering of the daughter of a priest is eaten but the meal-offering of a priest is not eaten. daughter of a priest can become disqualified but a priest does not become desacralized daughter of a priest may become impure by a corpse, but a priest may not become impure by a corpse A priest may eat from offerings of the most sacred order, but daughter of a priest may not eat from offerings of the most sacred order. What between a man and a woman? A man lets grow and rends but a woman does not let grow or rend A man can vow his son be a nazirite, but a woman cannot vow her son be a nazirite. A man is hanged but a woman is not hanged. A man is sold for his theft but a woman is not sold for her theft. And capital law, opens to acquit but does not open to find liable. monetary law, directs, based on one either to exempt, or to find liable. But capital law, directs based on one to acquit and based on two to find liable. monetary law, brings back either to exempt or to find liable. capital law, brings back to acquit but does not bring to find liable. monetary law, all may teach exempt or liable. capital law, all may teach acquit but not all may teach liable. monetary law, one who teaches liable may teach exempt and one who teaches exempt may teach liable. capital law, one who teaches liable may teach acquit, but one who teaches acquit may not return and teach liable. monetary law, judges during the daytime, and may conclude at night. capital law, judges during the daytime, and concludes in the daytime. monetary law, conclude on that same day, whether to exempt or to find liable. capital law, conclude on that same day to acquit the following day to liable. Therefore, does not judge neither on the eve of Shabbat nor the eve of a Festival. monetary law, the ritual impurity and purity, commence from the greatest capital law, commence from the side, All are fit to judge monetary law. Like this when Rabbi Akiva was walking along the road and came to a certain city, he inquired about lodging and they did not give him He said: Everything that God does, He does for the best. They sent to them Sinai takes precedence, everyone needs the owner of the wheat, Nevertheless, Rav Yosef did not accept as the Chaldean told him: You will preside two years. Rabba presided twenty-two years. Rav Yosef presided two and a half years. all those years that Rabba presided, did not even call a bloodletter to his home. And Rabbi Avin HaLevi said: What is that which is written: “” the God of Jacob and not the God of Abraham and Isaac? from here One who owns a beam should approach the thick portion of the beam. And Rabbi Avin HaLevi said: One who partakes of a meal at which a Torah scholar is present, it is as if he enjoyed the radiant splendor of the Divine Presence, as it is stated: “” Did they eat before God? Didn’t they eat before Moses? Rather, to tell you one who partakes in a meal at which a Torah scholar is present, it is as if he enjoyed the radiant splendor of the Divine Presence. And Rabbi Avin HaLevi said: One who takes leave from another should not say to him: Go in peace, but rather, Go to peace. As we see Jethro said to Moses: “” Moses ascended and was successful. David said to Absalom: “” went and was hanged. Rabbi Avin HaLevi also said: One who takes leave from a dead person should not say to him: Go to peace, but rather, Go in peace, as it is stated: “” Rabbi Levi bar Ḥiyya said: One who leaves the synagogue and enters the study hall and engages in Torah is privileged to receive the Divine Presence, as it is stated: “” Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Ashi said Rav said: Torah scholars have rest neither in this world nor in the World-to-Come, as it is stated: “” Rabbi Elazar said Rabbi Ḥanina said: Torah scholars increase peace in the world, as it is said: “” Do not read your children [<i>banayikh</i>], but your builders [<i>bonayikh</i>]. “” “” “” “”
